category: Register — which Sanskrit is being taught
label: WHICH SANSKRIT: the course teaches a spoken register, and the exam ladder behind it does not
note: Sanskrit-specific, and the first point a reader should look at. core/exam-levels.json records Sanskrit as basis 'editorial' with the caveat that this project teaches it AS A LIVING SPOKEN LANGUAGE so CEFR can-do descriptors apply, while 'a traditional syllabus is ordered by grammar and text rather than by communicative function, so the two ladders are not parallel'. That is load-bearing: every functional point in this file measures the spoken-revival register that Samskrita Bharati teaches, and NONE of it measures the traditional pariksha, which would ask for declension tables and a text. bhavān katham asti? and kuśalī asmi are spoken-revival forms; a classical text would not use them conversationally. A coverage number here is not progress toward a traditional examination and cannot become one.
